# Colin's 2025 Outside Memory

## Welcome Message

Welcome, Colin! We're thrilled to celebrate you as a power user of Outside Online's media properties. Over the past year, you've logged nearly 3,900 interactions across our platforms, and your passion for endurance sports and cycling culture has been truly inspiring to witness. This is your personalized year in review—a story of your engagement, your evolving interests, and the adventures you've pursued.

---

## Colin's 2025 Outside Memory

Your year with us tells the story of an athlete deeply committed to multi-sport endurance racing. You started strong in January 2025, exploring cycling events and registrations, but February marked a turning point—your engagement nearly quadrupled as you discovered the power of Trailforks and began planning adventures across multiple disciplines. This was the month you truly activated across our ecosystem.

Spring brought peak engagement in March and April, with 440 and 365 events respectively. During these months, you were voraciously consuming cycling content—diving deep into professional road racing analysis, following stars like **Tadej Pogačar**, **Jonas Vingegaard**, and **Egan Bernal** through their seasons. You were equally active registering for events across BikeReg, TriReg, and RunReg, suggesting you were gearing up for a busy race calendar. Your interests were crystallizing: grand tours and professional cycling analysis paired with your own competitive pursuits.

Summer brought a fascinating shift. After a dip in May and June (126 events in June), you experienced an explosion in August with 873 events—your highest engagement month of the year. This surge was driven largely by intensive use of the Trailforks App (953 total app events across the year), where you were actively exploring trails, posting to feeds, checking ride plans, and building your wishlist of regions. You were planning, discovering, and connecting with the trail community. Simultaneously, you continued your meticulous attention to professional cycling through VeloNews, reading pieces like "Our First Impressions of Zwift and TrainerRoad's New AI Integration" and staying connected to the tech side of training.

Fall and winter saw a gradual wind-down, which is natural—but telling. Your engagement patterns suggest you were either transitioning into different training phases or preparing for specific events. By December and January 2026, your activity had settled to quieter levels (74 and 97 events respectively), possibly reflecting seasonal shifts in racing or a focus on training rather than content consumption.

---

## Your Passions

• **Professional Road Cycling & Grand Tours** - You're deeply invested in elite cycling, with 13 engagements around Tour de France coverage and consistent attention to riders like Tadej Pogačar, Jonas Vingegaard, Egan Bernal, João Almeida, and Mikel Landa. Your interest in analysis-tagged content (8 engagements) shows you're not just following results—you're understanding the sport.

• **Multi-Sport Event Racing** - BikeReg (715 events) dominates your activity, but you're equally engaged across TriReg (139 events), RunReg (34 events), and SkiReg (15 events). You're a true multi-disciplinary athlete, registering for everything from cyclocross championships to triathlons to ski races.

• **Mountain Biking & Trail Exploration** - Your 953 interactions with the Trailforks App and 685 on the Trailforks website reveal a dedicated trail enthusiast. You're exploring regions like Phoenix, discovering routes like "Brown's Ranch Loop" and "Gnar Weasels Course," and actively engaging with the trail community through posts and comments.

• **Cycling Training & Performance Optimization** - Articles on nutrition (5 engagements) and pieces about TrainerRoad and Zwift integration show you're serious about the science of training. You're not just racing—you're optimizing every aspect of your preparation.

• **Gravel & Cyclocross Racing** - Your registrations span events like the "Arkansas Graveler," "Really Rad Festival of Cyclocross," and "Highlands Gran Fondo," indicating you're exploring the full spectrum of bike racing disciplines beyond just road and mountain.

• **Active Community Engagement** - Your use of Trailforks' social features (activity feeds, comments, posts to feed) shows you're not a passive consumer—you're building connections, sharing experiences, and contributing to the trail community.

---

## Reading Habits

Your reading patterns reveal a disciplined, strategic approach to content consumption. You're most active during evening and late-night hours—your peak engagement times cluster around 2–10 PM (with particular spikes at 10 PM, 4 PM, 3 PM, and 6 PM), suggesting you're reading during wind-down time or between training sessions. Saturdays are your most active day (674 events), which makes sense for an endurance athlete planning weekend adventures or catching up on the week's racing coverage.

Your content diet is heavily weighted toward cycling journalism, particularly from **Andrew Hood** and **Jim Cotton** (5 articles each from VeloNews), whose bylines appear consistently in your history. You're reading deep-dive analysis pieces, gear reviews (like the "First Look: Cannondale Revives The SuperX Name"), and training-focused content. The presence of tags like "behind-the-ride" (5 engagements) and "evergreen" (9 engagements) suggests you value both narrative storytelling and timeless, reference-worthy content that you can return to.

Your engagement with Outside Online itself (134 events) is meaningful but secondary to your registration and trail-exploration activities, indicating you're using our platform strategically—seeking specific information rather than browsing casually. Combined with your 579 unique articles read across 364 days, you're consuming roughly 1.6 articles per day on average, a sustainable pace that suggests you're selective and intentional about what you read.
